sections.heading: C2 — Following, merging, crossing and passing space
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Following, merging, crossing and passing space

FACT_ID: sec16-R01 | anchor: A03
When vulnerable users are not involved, the handbook advises a middle course between two hazards, with additional clearance toward the more dangerous side. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec16-R02 | anchor: A03
Address hazards separately when possible; if an opposing vehicle approaches while you intend to pass a bicycle, slow and let it pass first. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec16-R03 | anchor: A03
When passing a cyclist, preserve at least three feet of clearance and use the neighboring lane on a multilane road whenever possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec16-R04 | anchor: A03
Do not merge into an undersized gap; choose enough room to maintain a safe space cushion. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec16-R05 | anchor: A03
When crossing several lanes, change one lane at a time rather than trying to cross them all at once. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec16-R06 | anchor: A03
A crossing maneuver needs room to clear the whole road, while entry needs room to turn and accelerate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec16-R07 | anchor: A03
Stop partway across only in a median large enough to contain the entire vehicle without protruding into traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec16-R08 | anchor: A04
Before turning left across opposing traffic, ensure the intended path is not blocked by vehicles or pedestrians. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R09 | anchor: A04
Do not enter a blocked intersection even on green; blocking it can result in a ticket. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R10 | anchor: A04
Do not assume another driver will create a gap or turn because a signal is flashing; wait for the turn to begin and proceed only when safe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R11 | anchor: A04
A motorcycle’s signal may remain on from an earlier turn because it may not cancel automatically. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R12 | anchor: A04
Cross rail tracks only when you can clear them without stopping on the tracks. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R13 | anchor: A04
Pass only where signs and markings permit and there is enough space; the handbook generally recommends passing one vehicle at a time. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R14 | anchor: A04
The handbook’s passing example at 55 mph calls for roughly 10 seconds of clear opposing traffic and sight distance, with the driver still judging whether space is adequate. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R15 | anchor: A04
At 55 mph, a vehicle covers more than 800 feet in 10 seconds. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R16 | anchor: A04
When both vehicles in the example travel at 55 mph, together they cover over 1,600 feet during 10 seconds; uncertainty about adequate passing space calls for waiting. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R17 | anchor: A04
The handbook advises against beginning a pass within one-third mile of a view-blocking hill or curve because opposing traffic may be hidden. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R18 | anchor: A04
Passing near intersections, rail crossings or shopping-area entrances is dangerous because other road users can enter unseen or not expect opposing-lane traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R19 | anchor: A04
Before passing, look for roadway restrictions or traffic that could push another vehicle into the passing space. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec16-R20 | anchor: A05
People or bicycles near the road, a narrowed bridge, ice, potholes or other obstructions can reduce available passing space. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec16-R21 | anchor: A05
Do not pass unless there is room to return to the proper lane without relying on other drivers to make space. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec16-R22 | anchor: A05
Do not pass with a railroad crossing ahead. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec16-R23 | anchor: A05
Before returning after a pass, leave adequate clearance; the handbook uses seeing both passed-vehicle headlights in the rear-view mirror as a clearance cue. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec16-R24 | anchor: A05
Allow extra room for drivers with obstructed views at intersections or driveways. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec16-R25 | anchor: A05
Give extra room to drivers reversing into the road or entering and leaving parking spaces because they may not see you. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec16-R26 | anchor: A05
Drivers with obscured windows and pedestrians with faces hidden by hats or umbrellas may need extra space. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec16-R27 | anchor: A05
Allow additional room or caution around distracted people, including delivery workers, construction workers, inattentive children and drivers. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec16-R28 | anchor: A05
Give extra room to potentially confused drivers, such as those searching for addresses, slowing inexplicably or appearing unsure of direction. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec16-R29 | anchor: A05
If another driver attempts a pass without enough room, slow and allow a safe return rather than making the mistake worse. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec16-R30 | anchor: A05
If a driver suddenly needs to change lanes, slow to allow the merge when needed to avoid a collision. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0132]
